patch_description: The current constructor uses a symmetric ring layout which wastes space and a flawed one-pass radius scaling. I replace it with a hexagonal-lattice layout: 6 rows with counts [5,4,5,4,5,3] = 26 circles. With touching neighbors (dx = 2r, dy = √3·r), the binding constraints are horizontal (2r + 4dx = 10r ≤ 1) and vertical (2r + 5√3·r ≤ 1), giving r ≈ 0.0938 and a uniform sum of ~2.44 (vs. current 0.96). Then, instead of a one-pass pairwise shrink (which underestimates radii), I add a Gauss–Seidel *growth* refinement: each circle's radius is grown up to the minimum of its wall distance and (distance to neighbor − neighbor's radius), iterating until no circle can grow. This lets circles near walls and in the truncated last row expand into unused space, pushing the sum toward the 2.6+ regime while guaranteeing feasibility (radii only grow when locally valid, boundary distances are hard caps).
